title: Voice Model: Voice Preservation, AI-Stink Detection, and Voice Editing Protocol
body:
Voice is the hardest quality to preserve and the easiest to destroy. An agent that 'improves' text without understanding its voice will produce prose that is technically cleaner and functionally worse. The failure mode: an agent receives text with a distinctive voice, applies 'editorial improvements', and returns text that is more correct but less alive.

**What Voice Is:** Voice is the combination of qualities that make text feel written by a specific intelligence rather than generated from an average of all similar text. Voice consists of: sentence rhythm and variation (mixing short declarative with longer analytical, deliberate rhythm breaks); commitment level (how strongly claims are stated — high-commitment voice states things directly, hedging erases it); word choice specificity (the most precise word vs. the safest one); what the writer notices (selected details reveal the sensibility); what the writer does not say (omissions are as much voice as inclusions); characteristic structures (how paragraphs open and close, recurring structural moves).

**What Voice Is Not:** Not consistent grammar (grammar can be correct while voice is absent). Not consistent tone (tone can vary; voice persists through tone changes). Not the absence of casual language (casual language is a voice choice). Not the absence of technical language (technical precision is a voice choice).

**AI-Stink Detection Checklist:**

Structural AI-stink: opens a section with a rhetorical question; uses 'it is worth noting' or 'it is important to note'; opens with a definition the audience already knows; states the obvious before the non-obvious; ends with 'In conclusion...' or 'To summarize...'; uses transition sentences that only announce what comes next.

Vocabulary AI-stink: 'Delve into', 'unpack', 'navigate', 'explore' as verbs for intellectual activity; 'leverage' (use 'use'); 'holistic', 'robust', 'comprehensive', 'cutting-edge', 'game-changing', 'transformative'; 'in today's fast-paced world'; 'nuanced', 'multifaceted', 'complex' as filler adjectives.

Rhythm AI-stink: all paragraphs roughly the same length; all sentences roughly the same syntactic structure; no unexpected rhythm breaks; everything is the most predictable word choice.

Commitment AI-stink: hedges a claim that should be stated directly; smooths over a contradiction instead of naming it; three examples when one would be more forceful; an argument that leads to a conclusion but pulls back from stating it.

When AI-stink is detected: flag the specific phrase or pattern; state specifically what is wrong (which detection criterion it triggers); propose a specific fix; do not perform a blind rewrite.

**Voice Preservation Rules When Editing:** (1) Identify characteristic voice markers before editing — list them explicitly. (2) Only edit for the stated purpose — if the task is grammar correction, do not also change voice. (3) Do not change characteristic structures unless they violate doctrine. (4) After editing, verify that identified voice markers survive. (5) If restoring a voice marker conflicts with the edit goal, surface the conflict — do not silently choose one over the other.

**When Merging Text from Multiple Agents:** Identify the dominant voice in each section. Identify the target voice for the document from the voice pack or style pack. Normalize toward the target voice, not toward a generic neutral voice. Normalization to flat, neutral prose is the wrong outcome — if the normalization pass produces text with no distinctive voice characteristics, it has failed.

**Voice Pack Required Fields:** sentence length tendency; commitment level; characteristic vocabulary (with specific words); what the writing notices; what the writing trusts the reader to know; anti-targets (voice qualities this pack is defined against). Voice packs are 200-400 words.
